title: Getting Started
content:
Install TokenCap globally with npm:

```bash
npm install -g tokencap
```

Then run from your JS/TS project root:

```bash
tokencap make
```

This generates three files in your project root:

- `TOKENCAP.md` — compressed project snapshot (all languages)
- `TOKENCAP_GRAPH.md` — dependency graph (JS/TS projects)
- `TOKENCAP_MEMORY.md` — developer context memory (all projects)

For VS Code, install the TokenCap extension from the marketplace (publisher: VanshArora21). It auto-captures on every file save.

title: Configuration
content:
Create a `.tokencap.json` file in your project root to customize behavior:

```json
{
  "profile": "balanced",
  "outputPath": "TOKENCAP.md",
  "maxFiles": 90,
  "maxSourceBytes": 220000,
  "maxFileBytes": 14000,
  "maxDiffBytes": 50000,
  "includeGitDiff": true,
  "includeFileContents": true,
  "excludePatterns": ["node_modules/**", "dist/**", "build/**", "coverage/**"],
  "redactSecrets": true
}
```

Configuration is resolved in the following priority order: defaults → profile overrides → .tokencap.json → CLI flags.

title: Context Profiles
content:
TokenCap ships with context profiles tuned for different AI models and use cases.

| Profile | Max Files | Source Budget | Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `compact` | 45 | 90KB | Local LLMs, tight windows |
| `balanced` | 90 | 220KB | Default — most models |
| `deep` | 140 | 420KB | Complex codebases |
| `gpt-4o` | 80 | 150KB | OpenAI GPT-4o |
| `claude-3-5-sonnet` | 120 | 250KB | Anthropic Claude |
| `gemini-1.5-flash` | 200 | 600KB | Gemini Flash |
| `gemini-1.5-pro` | 400 | 1.2MB | Gemini Pro |
| `llama-3-8b` | 25 | 40KB | Local Llama |

Select a profile via CLI flag or `.tokencap.json`:

```bash
tokencap make --profile claude-3-5-sonnet
```

title: Smart Context Retrieval
content:
TokenCap moves from simply generating full codebase snapshots to retrieving exactly what matters. Ask a natural language question or request context by topic keyword, and the retrieval engine finds the relevant files, performs graph BFS, filters by token budget, and generates a tailored AI prompt.

### How it Works (Retrieval Engine)

```
Your question
  → Extract keywords ("auth", "login", "jwt")
  → Match to clusters (Authentication)
  → Score all files using Graph + Memory + Diff + Impact
  → BFS: find dependencies & dependents (up to 2 hops)
  → Rank by composite relevance score
  → Allocate token budget (default: 12,000)
  → Generate context.md + prompt.md
```

- **Multi-Source Retrieval** — Searches across your dependency graph (clusters, connections), developer memory (active tasks, decisions), git status (recent changes), and risk impact score to rank files by relevance.
- **Auto-Mode Detection** — Questions are parsed to auto-detect the retrieval intent. Keywords like "explain" auto-detect `architecture` mode, "review" or "verify" auto-detect `review` mode, and "debug" or "fix" auto-detect `debug` mode.
- **Graph BFS Traversal** — Traverses the dependency structure up to 2 hops from matching files to ensure all relevant helper modules, utilities, and parent controllers are included in the package.
- **Token-Budgeted Output** — Dynamically applies representation tiers (Full content, Structural outlines, AST summaries, or Reference Only) to fit the retrieved content into a strict token budget.

### Ask about any part of your codebase

```bash
tokencap ask "How does authentication work?"
tokencap ask "Explain invoice generation"
tokencap ask "debug login redirect"           # Auto-detects debug mode
tokencap ask "review payment flow"             # Auto-detects review mode
```

### Quick topic context

Generate topic-specific context manually using a keyword:

```bash
tokencap context auth
tokencap context payments
tokencap context dashboard
```

title: Project Knowledge Graph
content:
TokenCap scans all JS/TS source files and maps how they connect to each other.

```bash
tokencap graph
```

This generates `TOKENCAP_GRAPH.md` and exports graph data to `.tokencap/graph/`.

### Graph Intelligence & Visualization Features

- **Obsidian-Style Interactive Viewer (`--open`)** — Opens a self-contained, dark-mode, three-panel graph viewer in your default browser. Features zoom, pan, hover highlights, local graph mode (showing a selected node + direct dependencies/dependents), cluster filtering, and a right-side node inspector panel showing metadata, risk, and impact.
- **13 Node Classifications** — Categorizes files into `route`, `api`, `component`, `controller`, `service`, `database`, `middleware`, `config`, `utility`, `hook`, `package`, `test`, and `unknown` with distinct color representations.
- **4-Tier Risk Scoring** — Assigns a `CRITICAL`, `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, or `LOW` risk tier to each node based on connectivity, classification, and git modification status.
- **Graph Presets** — Simplifies running graph actions:
  - `--full` — Runs JSON export, AI narrative summary, graph diff, and opens the HTML viewer in your browser (combines `--json --ai --diff --open`).
  - `--minimal` — Exports only `graph-data.json`, `nodes.json`, and `edges.json`. No HTML, AI, or diff (fastest).
  - `--quiet` — Runs in the background and prints only a clean summary statistics block.
- **Cluster Detection** — Automatically groups code files into logical modules: Authentication, Payments, Dashboard, Database, API, Frontend, Config, Testing, and Utilities.
- **TOKENCAP.md Graph Summary** — Injects a `## Project Graph Summary` section containing key metrics (node/edge counts, high-risk files, clusters detected) into the main snapshot after every graph run.

**Supported file extensions:** `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`

**Import patterns parsed:**
- `import x from "./file"`
- `import { x } from "../file"`
- `export { x } from "./file"`
- `const x = require("./file")`

**Node classification:**

| Pattern | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `/app/`, `/pages/`, `page.*`, `route.*`, `layout.*` | `route` |
| `/api/` + `route.*` | `api` |
| Uppercase name, `/components/`, `/ui/`, `.tsx` | `component` |
| `/lib/`, `/services/`, `/utils/`, `/hooks/` | `service` |
| `schema.prisma`, `/models/`, `/db/`, `/database/` | `database` |
| `next.config.*`, `vite.config.*`, `tsconfig.*`, `package.json` | `config` |

**Note:** Only local relative imports are followed. External packages (react, lodash, etc.) are ignored.

title: Context Memory Layer
content:
Preserve your developer context across sessions.

Instead of a separate command, the context memory layer is automatically compiled whenever you run `tokencap make`.

This process:
1. Reads your developer notes from `.tokencap-notes.md` in your project root (auto-created if missing).
2. Combines them with live Git context (branch name + changed files).
3. Writes a structured `TOKENCAP_MEMORY.md` context file.

**Edit `.tokencap-notes.md` directly:**

```md
## Current Task
Fix login redirect after successful authentication.

## Developer Intent
Improve auth flow without changing the DB schema.

## Known Issues
- Session sometimes not ready before redirect.

## Constraints
- Do not modify Prisma schema.

## Decisions Made
- Using server-side session validation.

## Next Steps
- Test login flow.
- Check middleware.
```

title: AI Context Packing
content:
The Context Packing Engine is a budget-driven, importance-scoring compressor that fits codebases of any size into AI context windows. Instead of dumping every file in full (which can quickly overwhelm LLM token limits), it scores files based on import centrality, git modification history, and debug relevance.

```bash
tokencap pack
```

### Pack Modes

- **`review`** (Default) — Optimized for code reviews. Prioritizes recent git changes, main application entry points, and files with pending/recent diffs.
- **`debug`** — Optimized for troubleshooting. Prioritizes stack trace files, active debug logs, and immediate dependencies of failing modules.
- **`architecture`** — Optimized for system understanding. Excludes deep implementation details, providing high-level structural outlines and module interfaces.
- **`minimal`** — A lightweight context profile containing only git status, active tasks, recent change lists, and high-level module metadata.

### How it Compresses (Budget Engine)

TokenCap analyzes files and applies one of four representation tiers based on their importance score and remaining token budget:

- 🟢 **Full Content**: Critical files are written in full.
- 🟡 **Structural Outline**: Mid-importance files are trimmed to show only function signatures, class definitions, and structural layout using regex parsing.
- 🟠 **AST Summary**: Low-importance files are summarized into small, token-dense structural descriptions (~80 tokens).
- 🔴 **Reference Only**: Distant/utility files are represented as simple file paths with export counts to preserve structural awareness without wasting budget.

Generate a pack with a custom token budget:

```bash
tokencap pack --mode debug --budget 30000
```

title: AI Change Intelligence
content:
The Change Intelligence Engine goes beyond standard git diffs by analyzing changes semantically. It provides a deterministic, rule-based report outlining impact, risk, breaking changes, and testing suggestions.

```bash
tokencap diff
```

### Key Capabilities

1. **Semantic Layering** — Classifies modified files into functional layers like `Authentication`, `Payment`, `Database`, `API`, `Frontend`, `Security`, etc.
2. **Deterministic Risk Rating** — Computes risk levels (`LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `CRITICAL`) based on files touched, lines modified, database schema changes, or breaking change detections.
3. **Breaking Change Scanning** — Scans for common breaking patterns such as removed exports, function signature alterations, prisma field deletions, and `.env` modifications.
4. **Endpoint Capture** — Identifies added or modified HTTP routes/endpoints (e.g. Express, Next.js App Router) and suggests specific edge cases to test.
5. **Prompt Generator** — Produces ready-to-use markdown prompts for AI code review or PR summaries:
   - `--pr` generates a condensed pull request description.
   - `--prompt` generates a structured prompt guiding an LLM to review your changes.

Analyze staged changes or the last commit:

```bash
tokencap diff --staged
tokencap diff --last
```

title: Agent Intelligence Engine
content:
TokenCap evolves from a context generator to an AI Project Intelligence Platform by analyzing your repository and automatically generating a complete Agent Skill Pack.

### How it Works (8-Phase Pipeline)

The flagship command `tokencap agent` runs an automated 8-phase pipeline that sequences analysis through the following stages:

```
Tech Stack
  → Architecture
  → Project Rules
  → Risk Map
  → Review Groups
  → Agent Skills
  → Agent Pack
  → Machine-readable JSON
```

1. **Tech Stack** — Automatically identifies frontend, backend, database, testing frameworks, CI/CD tools, and primary languages.
2. **Architecture** — Maps high-level directory structure, core subsystems, key entry points, and architectural paradigms.
3. **Project Rules** — Captures coding standards, style guidelines, import conventions, and repository-specific patterns.
4. **Risk Map** — Flags highly volatile files, central utilities with cascading dependencies, and critical security pathways.
5. **Review Groups** — Identifies target review groups for components (e.g. Frontend Reviewers, Database Admins, Security Officers).
6. **Agent Skills** — Synthesizes discrete, execution-oriented guidelines instructing an AI agent exactly how to interact with your codebase.
7. **Agent Pack** — Formulates a single paste-ready markdown payload (`agent-pack.md`) optimized for LLM assistants.
8. **Machine-readable JSON** — Generates `agent.json` containing structured definitions and `agentInjectHooks` for future integrations.

### Generate Agent Skills

Create a complete Agent Skill Pack in your project root:

```bash
tokencap agent
```

This generates:
- `agent-pack.md` — A single paste-ready file for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Roo Code, and OpenHands.
- `agent.json` — Structured machine-readable output with `agentInjectHooks` for future `--inject` integrations (v0.9+).

### Focused Generation (Mode Flags)

Generate only specific phases of the pipeline using mode flags:

- `--full` — Runs the full 8-phase intelligence pipeline (default).
- `--architecture` — Generates a focused pack outlining tech stack and architecture mapping.
- `--rules` — Compiles focused coding rules, import conventions, and repository guidelines.
- `--skills` — Extracts targeted, execution-ready guidelines and code review requirements.

title: Project Brain
content:
TokenCap thinks in clusters, not just files. The flagship **Project Brain** (`tokencap brain`) allows you to query any part of your codebase to get a unified intelligence view including files, risk levels, architecture, dependencies, review groups, recent changes, and git timeline — all from a single command.

### How it Works

```
Your topic ("auth")
  → Load .tokencap/brain/knowledge.json   (built by tokencap make)
  → Fuzzy-match topic against cluster names and file paths
  → Resolve matching cluster + all intelligence views
  → Render to terminal in requested mode
```

### Brain Modes

- **Overview (Default)** — Displays files, risk level, review group, recent changes, and architecture chain.
- **Impact (`--impact`)** — Shows affected file/feature count, critical files, and risk levels.
- **Architecture (`--architecture`)** — Renders the dependency chain (what this cluster depends on / is used by) as an ASCII map.
- **Review (`--review`)** — Shows files in the review group and the reason for grouping.
- **Timeline (`--timeline`)** — Lists Git commit history (date + message) for cluster files.
- **Risk (`--risk`)** — Pinpoints high-risk areas, reason, and affected files.
- **Deps (`--deps`)** — Lists all direct depends-on and used-by edges.

### Example CLI Usage

```bash
tokencap brain auth                  # Full overview of auth cluster
tokencap brain payments --impact     # Impact analysis of payments changes
tokencap brain auth --architecture   # ASCII dependency chain
tokencap brain auth --timeline       # Git history timeline for auth
tokencap brain                       # Overview of all clusters with risk levels
```

title: Secret Redaction
content:
TokenCap automatically redacts secrets before writing any file content to disk. Redaction is enabled by default (`redactSecrets: true`).

**Patterns detected and redacted:**

- OpenAI API keys: `sk-...` → `[REDACTED_OPENAI_KEY]`
- GitHub PATs: `ghp_...`, `github_pat_...` → `[REDACTED]`
- Slack tokens: `xox...` → `[REDACTED]`
- AWS access keys: `AKIA...` → `[REDACTED]`
- Google API keys: `AIza...` → `[REDACTED]`
- Bearer tokens (≥20 chars)
- Generic variable assignments: `api_key=`, `token=`, `secret=`, `password=`, `passwd=`, `pwd=`

To disable redaction (not recommended for shared snapshots):

```json
{ "redactSecrets": false }
```

title: CLI Reference
content:
TokenCap provides a simplified 10-command CLI for generating AI-ready project context, retrieving semantic files from questions, analyzing code changes, debugging, packing token-budgeted prompt files, generating AI Agent Skill Packs, and querying unified cluster intelligence.

---

# Installation

Install TokenCap globally:

```bash
npm install -g tokencap
```

Verify installation:

```bash
tokencap --version
```

---

# tokencap brain

Project Brain — unified intelligence query about any part of your codebase.

```bash
tokencap brain <topic>
```

## Options

* `--impact` — Show affected file/feature count, critical files, and risk level.
* `--architecture` — Render dependency chain ASCII view for the cluster.
* `--review` — Show review group files and reason for grouping.
* `--timeline` — Show git commit history (date + message) for cluster files.
* `--risk` — Show risk areas and affected files.
* `--deps` — Show full depends-on and used-by lists.

---

# tokencap agent

Generate an Agent Skill Pack and structured config for AI agents.

```bash
tokencap agent
```

## Options

* `--full` — Run the full 8-phase pipeline (default)
* `--architecture` — Focused generation of architecture details
* `--rules` — Focused generation of project coding rules and conventions
* `--skills` — Focused generation of agent skill definitions and instructions

---

# tokencap ask

Smart context retrieval from a natural language question.

```bash
tokencap ask "How does authentication work?"
```

## Options

* `--mode <name>` — review | debug | architecture (override auto-detected mode)
* `--budget <number>` — Custom token budget. Default: 12000
* `--json` — Also export context.json
* `--no-prompt` — Skip generating the prompt.md file

---

# tokencap context

Manual context generation by topic keyword.

```bash
tokencap context auth
```

## Options

* `--mode <name>` — Override mode: review | debug | architecture
* `--budget <number>` — Custom token budget. Default: 8000
* `--json` — Also export context.json
* `--prompt` — Generate prompt.md file

---

# tokencap make

Generate a complete AI-ready project context snapshot.

```bash
tokencap make
```

## What it does

Scans your repository and generates the main snapshot files:

* `TOKENCAP.md` — main workspace snapshot containing file content, Git context, diffs, TODOs, and redacted secrets
* `TOKENCAP_GRAPH.md` — project knowledge graph
* `TOKENCAP_MEMORY.md` — developer context memory

## Options

* `--profile <name>` — compact | balanced | deep | gpt-4o | claude-3-5-sonnet | gemini-1.5-flash | gemini-1.5-pro | llama-3-8b
* `--max-files <n>` — Maximum number of files to include
* `--max-bytes <n>` — Total source byte budget
* `--max-file-bytes <n>` — Per-file content byte limit
* `--max-diff-bytes <n>` — Git diff byte budget
* `--no-diff` — Skip Git diff snippets
* `--no-contents` — Skip selected file contents (structure outline only)

---

# tokencap graph

Analyze the code knowledge graph and dependency topology.

```bash
tokencap graph
```

## Presets & Options

* `--open` — Opens the Obsidian-style three-panel interactive viewer in default browser
* `--full` — Runs full intelligence (JSON export + AI narrative summary + graph diff + viewer)
* `--minimal` — Generates only JSON exports (`graph-data.json`, `nodes.json`, `edges.json`)
* `--quiet` — Suppresses verbose logs and shows only a clean stats block
* `--diff` — Generates graph-diff.md comparing current relationships vs last run
* `--ai` — Generates AI narrative summary only
* `--json` — Exports raw JSON files to `.tokencap/graph/`

---

# tokencap diff

Perform a semantic Change Intelligence analysis on your edits.

```bash
tokencap diff
```

## Options

* `--staged` — Analyze only staged changes (prior to a commit)
* `--last` — Analyze changes in the last commit (HEAD~1..HEAD)
* `--pr` — Generate a pull request summary description
* `--prompt` — Generate an optimized AI code review prompt
* `--json` — Output machine-readable JSON analysis

---

# tokencap debug

Unified debug session management.

```bash
tokencap debug --start
```

## Debug Flags

* `--start` — Start a new debug session (append '-- <command>' to run command and auto-capture stderr, failed tests, and traces)
* `--end` — End the active debug session, compile final handoff report, and archive it
* `--log "message"` — Add a timestamped update or discovery note to the active session timeline

## Example Workflow

```bash
tokencap debug --start -- npm test
# (investigate and edit files based on active debug notes)
tokencap debug --log "Reverted middleware changes - test still failing"
tokencap debug --end
# (paste .tokencap/debug/active.md into your AI assistant)
```

---

# tokencap pack

Generate a token-budgeted, importance-scored context pack for LLM prompts.

```bash
tokencap pack
```

## Options

* `--mode <name>` — Select compression mode: review | debug | architecture | minimal
* `--budget <number>` — Set maximum token budget. Default: 20000

---

# tokencap watch

Automatically regenerate TokenCap snapshots on file saves.

```bash
tokencap watch
```

## Options

* `--debounce <ms>` — Milliseconds to wait after a file change before regenerating. Default: 30000

---

# Recommended Workflow

### Understand any part of your codebase instantly (v0.9)

```bash
tokencap brain auth
```

---

### Teach an AI Agent (v0.8)

```bash
tokencap agent
```

---

### Ask about any part of your codebase (v0.7)

```bash
tokencap ask "How does authentication work?"
```

---

### Quick topic context (v0.7)

```bash
tokencap context payments
```

---

### Daily Development

```bash
tokencap watch
```

---

### Before Asking AI

```bash
tokencap make
```

---

### During Debugging

```bash
tokencap debug --start -- npm test

tokencap debug --log "Tested middleware"

tokencap debug --end
```

---

### Before Deployment

```bash
tokencap diff
```

title: VS Code Extension
content:
The TokenCap VS Code extension brings all functionality directly into your editor.

**Installation:** Search for `TokenCap` by `VanshArora21` in the VS Code Extensions panel, or install the VSIX package manually.

**Auto Capture:** After installing, TokenCap starts watching your workspace immediately. Every time you save a file, it waits 30 seconds (configurable) then regenerates all three snapshot files.

**Status Bar:** A `$(files) TokenCap • HH:MM` item appears in the status bar showing your last snapshot time. Click it to open the command menu.

**Command Menu (Quick-Pick):**
- Make Snapshot Now
- Open TokenCap Snapshot
- Toggle Auto Capture ON/OFF
- Create Config File

**VS Code Settings:**

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tokencap.autoCapture` | `true` | Auto-regenerate on save |
| `tokencap.debounceMs` | `30000` | Wait time after save |
| `tokencap.outputPath` | `TOKENCAP.md` | Output file path |
| `tokencap.profile` | `balanced` | Context profile |
| `tokencap.maxFiles` | `90` | Max files in snapshot |
| `tokencap.maxSourceBytes` | `220000` | Source byte budget |
| `tokencap.maxFileBytes` | `14000` | Per-file byte limit |
| `tokencap.maxDiffBytes` | `50000` | Diff byte budget |
| `tokencap.includeGitDiff` | `true` | Include git diffs |
| `tokencap.includeFileContents` | `true` | Include file contents |
